title: Ibn Battuta: Anatolia, the Golden Horde and Constantinople, 1330–32
summary: By Aydhab, Cairo and Syria to Latakia, by sea to Anatolia and across it to Sinop, over the Black Sea to the Golden Horde, and with the khan's Byzantine wife to Constantinople and back to the Volga. Dunn's dates; the Rihla's are 1332–34.

events.label: The Young Akhis
events.text: In every Turkmen town of Anatolia he was lodged by the akhis, guilds of young unmarried tradesmen who pooled each day's earnings to feed and house any traveller who came. Nowhere in the world, he says, were men so solicitous for strangers.

events.label: Bursa and Iznik: Orhan and Bayalun
events.text: At Bursa the sultan was Orhan, son of Osman, the greatest of the Turkmen kings. Iznik, taken from the Byzantines that year, was half empty; his wife Bayalun Khatun lived there in command of its few men.

events.label: The khan's moving city
events.text: He found the camp of Öz Beg Khan of the Golden Horde on the move near Beshtau, a vast city of waggons travelling with its mosques and markets.

events.label: Constantinople
events.text: He came with the khatun Bayalun, the khan's Byzantine wife, going home to her father's court to give birth, and had an audience of the emperor. Dunn's year; the Rihla's is 1334.
